findings.source: Both induced homomorphisms called inverse to each other.
findings.reason: Their domains and codomains differ: A→B∨ andB→A∨; dimension equality proves both are isomorphisms, not mutual inverses.
findings.resolution: English retains printed wording; Chinese says both maps are isomorphisms and adjacent note explains their domains do not permit saying mutual inverses.

findings.source: Representatives and independent list end at x_r after the quotient list ends at x_s.
findings.resolution: English preserves x_r; Chinese uses x_s with adjacent note.
findings.reason: The quotient family is indexed 2,...,s; r is not the family length.

findings.source: The alternative decomposition is described as having d terms, then written with s terms.
findings.resolution: English preserves d; Chinese uses s with adjacent note.
findings.reason: The displayed alternative decomposition and ensuing inequalities r≤s and r=s consistently use s.

findings.source: The torsion quotient term uses bar e_j although a_{s+j}=q_j and the first s coefficients are units.
findings.resolution: English preserves bar e_j; Chinese uses bar e_{s+j} with adjacent note.
findings.reason: Images bar e_1,...,bar e_s vanish; q_j belongs to e_{s+j}.

findings.source: The filtration M=M_1⊃...⊃M_r=0 is assigned length r.
findings.resolution: English preserves r; Chinese says r−1 with adjacent note.
findings.reason: There are r−1 consecutive simple quotients; page172 sums from1 to r−1 and assigns length1 to each simple module.

findings.source: The prose says the M_j component is f_j^i(x).
findings.resolution: Both texts preserve the prose; Chinese adjacent note says it is −f_j^i(x).
findings.reason: Page175 defines the relation tuple with minus, necessary for x and its image to identify in quotient.

findings.source: The inverse-limit notation sentence says transition maps f_j^i whereas preceding inverse system was defined with f_i^j.
findings.resolution: Both texts retain printed notation; translator review records discrepancy.
findings.reason: Enlarged original confirms printed indices. The sentence only omits the family from notation; no inferred reversal of actual projection maps was introduced.

findings.source: Finite sequence target is product n=1..N C_n.
findings.resolution: Both texts preserve source display, Chinese adjacent note supplies target n=1..N−1, component c_n−u_{n+1,n}c_{n+1}.
findings.reason: For N=1 printed1−u has zero kernel but finite inverse limit is C_1. Corrected map has compatible tuples as kernel and is surjective by backward recursion.

findings.source: Full-rank subgroup M of permutation lattice is claimed to have equivariantly permuted basis.
findings.resolution: Both preserve source; Chinese visible note gives nonstable full-rank counterexample and explicitly declines a complete repair.
findings.reason: For swap of two points, M=2Z[s1]⊕Z[s2] has full rank but is not stable; conclusion would imply stability. No claim that adding stability alone suffices.

findings.source: The hint says 0≤n_{j,k}≤d−1 without restricting k.
findings.resolution: Both preserve expression; Chinese note restricts it to k<j and gives1≤n_{j,j}≤d.
findings.reason: n_{j,j} is positive minimal and d is eligible; M=M1,d=1 gives n_{j,j}=1, disproving applying printed bound to diagonal.

findings.source: Exercise18(b) gives M but prints T_p(A).
findings.resolution: English retains A; Chinese says T_p(M) with adjacent note.
findings.reason: Given group is M; Tate-module construction applied to that group.

findings.source: Exercise23 says for any module N, Hom(N,−) commutes with directed direct limits.
findings.resolution: English preserves any N; Chinese adds finitely presented and exact-source note, referring to26.
findings.reason: Exercise26 gives sufficient finite-presentation condition. For infinite free N=⊕Z and M_i finite free summands with colimit N, identity N→N cannot factor through any M_i, so arbitrary assertion fails.

findings.source: Exercise28 prints L(ca)=L(c)L(a) while explaining k-linearity and filtration preservation.
findings.resolution: English preserves product; Chinese says cL(a) with adjacent note.
findings.reason: Scalar linearity identity is L(ca)=cL(a). Original product imposes an additional constraint not entailed by k-linearity; note explicitly treats intended linearity definition.

findings.source: Exercise29(a) says unique potential component in n_1 is x_nn.
findings.resolution: English retains x_nn; Chinese says x_1n with adjacent note.
findings.reason: First n−1 diagonals vanish, leaving right upper corner. x_nn belongs to main diagonal and is zero in strictly upper triangular matrices.

notes: Verified is a record of accurate visual reading and faithful transcription/translation with visible source caveats; it does not assert every printed mathematical claim is true.

Greek exponent nu on164 retained after enlarged original review. Source notation mod, sums, author identification equality and limit notation retained; mathematical equivalents were not called OCR errors.
The source issue on181 is resolved as a known inadequate assertion with counterexample. No reconstruction of a complete intended correction is claimed.
